title: Awake and Sing! by Clifford Odets at Sea Dog Theater #awakeandsing #s...
transcript: Awake and Sing! by Clifford Odets is 90 years old, but it's alive and well at a church in Gramercy. Sea Dog Theater's 90th anniversary production of this Depression-era family drama is a stark and well-acted exercise in making good use of a nontraditional space. Staged around a long wooden table and sprinkled with dramatically underscored transitional tableaus throughout, there's an apt moodiness that permeates the production. The story itself is about a family in the Bronx ripe with disagreements in ideologies, which is where most of the dramatic tension comes from. The adult children, being in their 20s, are grappling with big aspirations for their self-determination. Their parents, particularly their mother, is wise to these ideals, having made her own sacrifices to live even a remotely respectable life. This tension crystallizes over the course of the 100 minutes, and it's definitely a slow burn. But even before I was very conceptually or emotionally invested, the strong performances, close physical proximity, and interesting direction were captivating from the jump. It took some getting used to the echo that's present in the cavernous space, but once I was acquainted with that, I really enjoyed the site-specific nature of this piece. Awake and Sing! is running through November 8th. With that, another program for my collection.
